title.narrative: Health Emergency Preparedness, Response and Resilience Program Using the Multiphase Programmatic Approach

description.narrative: The Development Objective (DO) is to strengthen health system resilience and multisectoral preparedness and response to health emergencies in Eastern and Southern Africa.

The development objective of the Health Emergency Preparedness, Response, and Resilience Program Using the Multiphase Programmatic Approach (MPA) Project is to strengthen health system resilience and multisectoral preparedness and response to health emergencies in Eastern and Southern Africa. There are four components to the project, the first component being strengthening the preparedness and resilience of regional and national health systems to manage health emergencies. This component will finance capacity strengthening of essential institutions, and activities that directly contribute to the resilience of the health systems to cope with HEs and are complementary to other health systems strengthening (HSS). This will have four subcomponents: (i) multisectoral and cross-border planning, financing, and governance; (ii) health workforce development, including a focus on identifying and addressing gender gaps in career progression; (iii) access to quality health commodities, including building capacity for local vaccine and pharmaceutical manufacturing, based on the lessons learned from the challenges in accessing COVID-19 vaccines in the region; and (iv) information systems for HEs and the digitalization. The second component is the improving the detection of and response to HEs through a multisectoral approach. the third component is the program management. The component will finance expenditures related to M&E, the program leaning agenda including building a body of evidence on gender in PPR, and program implementation and coordination. Finally, the fourth component is the contingent emergency response component. This component will facilitate access to rapid financing by allowing for the reallocation of uncommitted project funds in the event of a natural disaster in a country, either by a formal declaration of a national emergency or upon a formal request from the government.

title.narrative: Countries that have national clinical case management guidelines for priority health events, and these guidelines are being implemented at the national level with project support
Points of entry supported per country to develop Public Health Emergency Contingency Plans
Countries where an essential health services package is newly approved or revised, including non-communicable diseases, mental health, and maternal and reproductive health services.
Countries reaching an average score of 3.5 in at least 3 JEE core capacity areas in each axis (Prevent, Detect, and Respond)
Countries that have achieved Level 4 of Joint External Evaluation indicator R5.3 ("Community Engagement")
Countries that have at least one field epidemiologist who has completed a minimum 1-year program in at least 90% of 1st-level administrative divisions (e.g. province)
Countries that have signed protocols to promote cross border response
Countries that have trained at least 1 health official in at least 90% of second-level administrative divisions (e.g. district) on IDSR
Countries where 60% of health events met all three 7-1-7 targets
Countries where 80% of project-supported laboratories have achieved a 3-star rating or higher during a SLIPTA audit
Countries with a national multi sectoral action plan for One Health that is costed and financed
Countries that have conducted a multisectoral simulation exercise, or an intra- or after-action review (within WHO-recommended timelines) for a health emergency that has occurred
Countries that have developed a RCCE plan and standard operating procedure which applies to both routine and emergency contexts, and accounts for gender dimensions of RCCE
Countries that have established an incident management system and have designated at least 1 health official in 90% of 2nd-level administrative divisions (e.g. district) to serve as incident manager.
Countries with at least 1 trained and functional rapid response team in at least 90% of first-level administrative divisions (e.g. province)
Countries that have developed or updated a multisectoral National Action Plan for Health Security.
People receiving quality health, nutrition, and population services
